question: A staff member realises she has pasted regulated customer records into her personal Claude account rather than the company's managed workspace. Which sequence is correct?
options: A) Redo the work in the managed workspace; delete the affected conversations as the response team directs; stop using the personal account for this work; report the incident through the escalation path the policy names.

B) Delete the affected conversations as the response team directs; stop using the personal account for this work; report the incident through the escalation path the policy names; redo the work in the managed workspace.

C) Stop using the personal account for this work; report the incident through the escalation path the policy names; delete the affected conversations as the response team directs; redo the work in the managed workspace.

D) Report the incident through the escalation path the policy names; redo the work in the managed workspace; delete the affected conversations as the response team directs; stop using the personal account for this work.
correct_answers: C) Stop using the personal account for this work; report the incident through the escalation path the policy names; delete the affected conversations as the response team directs; redo the work in the managed workspace.
explanations: Getting the work done comes ahead of every governance step, and the incident is reported last of all. By then the conversations have already been deleted without direction and the exposure has gone unreported.

Deletion is placed before the incident has been reported, so there is nobody yet to direct it. Destroying the record ahead of the report also removes the evidence the response team needs to scope what was exposed.

Correct. Containment comes first, so no further regulated data is exposed; the incident is then reported through the path the policy names, so the response team can assess it; remediation such as deletion follows their direction rather than preceding it; and the work resumes in the approved workspace.

Reporting comes first here, but the exposure is left running: the work is redone and conversations deleted while the personal account is still in use for regulated material, and it is stopped only at the very end.
